summary: The audit checks the pre-clerkship courses for quarters 1 to 6, the ten core clerkships, six units each of Selective I and Selective II, Selective III, six units of elective clerkships, at least 99 units of 300-series clerkship training in all, MED 397A (Preparation for Residency), INDE 297, and 235 units overall. Checked by hand: which core clerkships you finish within your first 12 periods, the Mini-CPX, CPX and USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK exams, and the scholarly concentration (declaring it, 12 units, a written report and a presentation). Units do not transfer into the MD.

b1yjAnki.why: "Students must complete at least six units / four weeks (of any 3**-series clerkships) to reach the minimum of 66 weeks / 99 units of clerkship training." The 99-unit total spans the core, selective and elective clerkship sections, so it is a hand-checked item. The 99-unit clerkship total is now a program total. The 300-series clerkships are the clinical departments' courses (ANES, CTS, DERM, EMED, FAMMED, MED, NENS, NSUR, OBGYN, OPHT, ORTHO, OTOHNS, PATH, PEDS, PSYC, RAD, RADO, SURG, UROL); their Medical Scholars Research (370), Graduate Research (399) and Curricular Practical Training (390) courses are numbered in the 300s but are not clerkships, and neither are other departments' 300-level courses.

mBRiAc5s.why: "All students must declare a concentration using the Medical Education Platform (MEP) by September 1st of their second year of study." "Students must choose one (1) area of study from a Foundation area listed below and complete 12 units of coursework" "Up to 6 of the 12 units can come from one of the application areas" "students must also complete two (2) non-course requirements": "Students must submit a written report of their scholarly work by June 1 of their graduating year." "Students must present their research and scholarly work by June 1 of their graduating year." The areas have no course lists, so the 12 units are moved in by the student.
